newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-O'NEAL COSTS LAKERS TITLE.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-O'NEAL COSTS LAKERS TITLE.

text.p: Shaquille O'Neal cost the Los Angeles Lakers any chance at the Pacific Division title when he missed two free throws with 1.2 seconds left, allowing the Portland Trail Blazers to escape with a 100-96 victory on Sunday.

O'Neal was fouled after rebounding a missed drive by teammate Nick Van Exel. With the Lakers trailing 98-96, O'Neal -- a 48 percent foul shooter -- missed the first attempt. He missed the second shot on purpose, but Portland's Cliff Robinson rebounded and made a pair of clinching free throws.
"These guys wanted to play us in the first round and now they've got us," O'Neal said. "I went for the score and I thought they weren't going to call it and I just missed the free throws."

In Cleveland, the Washington Bullets made the playoffs for the first time in nine years as Calbert Cheaney scored five points in the final three minutes of an 85-81 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Bullets (44-38) nosed out the Cavaliers (42-40) for the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference and a first-round matchup with the Chicago Bulls. Washington ended the longest current playoff drought of any team.
Chris Webber had 23 points and 17 rebounds and Rod Strickland added 19 points and nine assists for the Bullets

At Indiana, Grant Hill scored 35 of his career-high 38 points after halftime as the Detroit Pistons snapped a four-game losing streak and finished fifth in the Eastern Conference with a 124-120 overtime victory over the Indiana Pacers.
Hill made 11-of-16 shots after the break and finished with seven rebounds and seven assists. Lindsey Hunter had 30 points and Terry Mills chipped in with 24 off the bench.
Rik Smits had 29 points and Reggie Miller added 27 for Indiana, which completed its season a disappointing 39-43 and missed the playoffs for the first time since 1989.

In Milwaukee, Vin Baker made all 13 of his shots from the field en route to 31 points as the Milwaukee Bucks used red-hot shooting to defeat Charlotte, 120-100, knocking the Hornets into the sixth playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.
Baker, who added 11 rebounds and five assists, came within two field goals of tying Wilt Chamberlain's 30-year-old NBA record of 15 field goals without a miss.
Armon Gilliam made 10-of-11 shots from the field and scored 23 points for Milwaukee.
Five Hornets scored in double figures.

At New Jersey, Jim Jackson recorded his second career triple double with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists as the New Jersey Nets ended their first season under John Calipari with a 108-92 victory over the playoff-bound Atlanta Hawks.

The Hawks finished the regular season with a 56-26 record, their best since a 57-25 mark in 1993-94. Atlanta is the fourth seed in the East and will play fifth seed Detroit in the first round of the playoffs.
The Nets finished 26-56, the third worst mark in the East, in Calipari's first year.
It was a four-game drop from last year and New Jersey's worst mark since an identical 26-56 mark in 1990-91.
Jackson hit 10-of-16 shots from the field and set a career-high in assists.
In Sacramento, Greg Foster and John Stockton each hit a pair of free throws in the final minute to lift the Utah Jazz to their 64th win of the season, a 113-109 defeat of the Sacramento Kings.
Karl Malone added 18 points and six rebounds and Stockton finished with 17 points and 14 assists for Utah.
The Jazz open their series against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday.

In San Antonio, Hakeem Olajuwon scored 27 points and Charles Barkley added 22 as the Houston Rockets posted their second-highest win total with a 103-99 defeat of the San Antonio Spurs, who completed their most disappointing NBA season.

Clyde Drexler added 16 points for the Rockets, who locked up the third seed in the Western Conference but have the second-best record via tiebreakers. Houston finished with 57 wins, one less than the 1993-94 club that won the NBA title.
The Rockets, who will have homecourt edge in the West against every team except Midwest Division champion Utah, will play the Minnesota Timberwolves in the first round of the playoffs.
In Boston, Damon Stoudamire scored 32 points as the Toronto Raptors notched their 30th win with a 125-94 rout of the Boston Celtics in the season finale for both teams.
Doug Christie scored 27 points for the Raptors (30-52), who made a nine-game improvement over their first season.
